article.title: Physicists Create First All-Optical Photonic Time Crystal, Halving Terahertz Light Losses
article.summary: A France-Germany team built the first all-optical photonic time crystal, cutting terahertz photon losses roughly in half and opening a path toward new lasers.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

Researchers from École Polytechnique, Collège de France, and Germany's Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf (HZDR) have built the first all-optical photonic time crystal, a metamaterial whose optical properties are modulated in time rather than in space, according to [École Polytechnique](https://www.polytechnique.edu/en/press-room/press-releases/shaping-light-never-photonic-time-crystals). The work, published in [Nature](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10825-9) on July 29, 2026, as "Plasmonic metamaterial time crystal," demonstrated that driving the device hard enough cuts photon dissipation by roughly half rather than adding to it, according to [HZDR](https://www.hzdr.de/db/Cms?pNid=99&pOid=78295).

## What We Know

- The device consists of micrometer-scale gold crenellated structures separated from an indium-antimony semiconductor layer by an insulating layer, according to [École Polytechnique](https://www.polytechnique.edu/en/press-room/press-releases/shaping-light-never-photonic-time-crystals).
- Its reflectivity is modulated on picosecond timescales, fast enough to periodically reshape how the metamaterial interacts with terahertz light, according to [HZDR](https://www.hzdr.de/db/Cms?pNid=99&pOid=78295).
- Terahertz frequencies sit roughly 1,000 times faster than the frequencies electronic components operate at, according to [ScienceDaily](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/07/260731034131.htm).
- The ultrafast, strong modulation needed to reach the photonic-time-crystal regime was driven by TELBE, a superradiant terahertz source at HZDR's ELBE accelerator, according to [HZDR](https://www.hzdr.de/db/Cms?pNid=99&pOid=78295).
- "TELBE's unique ability to generate high-field, phase-stable terahertz pulses was critical," said Jan-Christoph Deinert, coordinator of the TELBE facility at HZDR, according to [École Polytechnique](https://www.polytechnique.edu/en/press-room/press-releases/shaping-light-never-photonic-time-crystals).
- "The THz range represents the frontier between electronic and photonic technologies," said Yannis Laplace, an assistant professor at École Polytechnique's Laboratory of Irradiated Solids, according to [EurekAlert!](https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/1138063).
- "By extending photonic crystals from space to time, we open a new dimension for light control—and a novel path toward amplification and lasing," said Tingwen Guo, the PhD student who is the paper's lead author, according to [École Polytechnique](https://www.polytechnique.edu/en/press-room/press-releases/shaping-light-never-photonic-time-crystals).
- Beyond the roughly 50 percent figure reported in the university and lab press releases, the Nature paper itself describes the effect as "emergent gain" that reduced plasmonic losses "by more than 50%," arising from "strong (near-unity) and coherent (sub-optical cycle) periodic driving of the plasmonic metamaterial," according to [Nature](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10825-9).
- The collaboration also drew on Thales' Laboratoire Albert Fert and École Polytechnique's Physics of Interfaces laboratory, according to [École Polytechnique](https://www.polytechnique.edu/en/press-room/press-releases/shaping-light-never-photonic-time-crystals).

## What We Don't Know

- The press materials describe plasmonic lasing as an application the team expects to become experimentally achievable, but none of the released materials specify a timeline or an experimental demonstration of an actual laser built on the effect.
- The full author list beyond the named lead author, Laplace, and Deinert was not consistently reported across the outlets reviewed, and this article does not attempt to enumerate the complete co-author roster.
- It remains unclear from the available materials how the ultrafast modulation techniques used at TELBE, a large accelerator-based facility, might eventually be miniaturized for practical devices outside a research lab.

## Analysis

Yannis Laplace, the École Polytechnique assistant professor quoted above, framed the terahertz band as sitting at a technological boundary rather than fully served by either conventional electronics or visible-light photonics, according to [EurekAlert!](https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/1138063). A time-domain analog of the photonic crystal — a class of materials long used to control light by patterning its refractive index in space — gives researchers a new tool for shaping terahertz light on the same timescale as its own oscillation cycle. Whether that translates into practical terahertz light sources, detectors, or lasers will depend on follow-up experiments beyond the initial demonstration reported in Nature.
